business.name: Harper IT Services
business.description: Small IT company providing managed services, break-fix, networking and equipment supply.
business.goal: Grow profitably without increasing owner stress.
business.concern: Flat revenue, customer churn, late payments and too much owner workload.

turns: The business has not really grown for three years.
We gained about 12 customers but lost 10.
Most who left said our price was too high. Six moved to cheaper managed service providers.
Managed services is our strongest margin and recurring revenue.
We do monitoring, support, backups and security, but we don't give clients a monthly report showing what we actually do.
My wife spends about 20 hours a week chasing payments and doing customer administration.
I was thinking of hiring an admin person and cutting our prices to win more customers.
Actually, the biggest thing I want is less owner stress without reducing profit.

business.name: Example Paint Distribution
business.goal: Build stronger brand pull and sustainable reseller demand.
business.concern: Good margins but dealers hesitate to promote the brand.

turns: The business is actually quite profitable.
Our main issue is that established brands dominate attention and dealers don't push our product.
Dealers tell us customers ask for established brands by name.
We offer attractive dealer margins but many still don't actively promote us.
We spend a lot of time telling dealers that our quality is good.
I am considering doubling the dealer incentive and increasing advertising.
I don't know whether more incentives will create customer demand or just pay dealers more.
I want to know what I should prove before spending more.

business.name: Example Retailer
business.description: One successful retail store with loyal customers and healthy margins.
business.goal: Decide whether a second location is genuinely ready and sensible.
business.concern: Considering a second store because the first is performing very well.

turns: Sales and margins are strong and customer loyalty is excellent.
The store manager runs most day-to-day operations.
I still handle supplier negotiations, cash decisions and unusual customer issues.
I believe a second store should work because the first store is successful.
I have not tested whether the first store performs for 30 days without me.
The second location would use about 40% of our available cash.
If it fails badly, we could survive but it would put pressure on the first store.
I am leaning toward opening, but I want to know whether I am seeing evidence or just confidence.
